bug_report_content:
id: 61
status: Fixed
summary: Type checker misses annotations on functions defined within functions
labels: ['Type-Defect', 'Priority-Medium']
stars: 7
commentCount: 7
Comment 0 (2009-11-25): What steps will reproduce the problem? 1. Compile the following code under --warning_level VERBOSE var ns = {}; /** @param {string=} b */ ns.a = function(b) {} function d() { ns.a(); ns.a(123); } 2. Observe that the type checker correctly emits one warning, as 123 doesn't match the type {string} 3. Now compile the code with ns.a defined within an anonymous function, like so: var ns = {}; (function() { /** @param {string=} b */ ns.a = function(b) {} })(); function d() { ns.a(); ns.a(123); } 4. Observe that a warning is emitted for calling ns.a with 0 parameters, and not for the type error, as though the @param declaration were ignored. What version of the product are you using? On what operating system? r15 Please provide any additional information below. This sort of module pattern is common enough that it strikes me as worth supporting. One last note to make matters stranger: if the calling code isn't itself within a function, no warnings are emitted at all: var ns = {}; (function() { /** @param {string=} b */ ns.a = function(b) {} })(); ns.a(); ns.a(123);
Comment 1 (2009-12-03): thanks for the report. I vaguely recall there was a very specific reason why this case wasn't handled, but I think that reason might have gone away. I'll play with it again and report back.
Comment 2 (2010-09-18): notice that if you define ns.a in a local scope, and use it in a later scope, this will now work. i'm still working on the case where you define ns.a in a local scope and call it from a global scope.
Comment 3 (2010-10-01): Nick, this specific issue is fixed any reason not to close this?
Comment 4 (2010-10-01): nope, the specific issue is not fixed. did you read my last comment?
Comment 5 (2010-10-01): I understand now. #3 is fixed now but not the call from global scope.
Comment 6 (2012-10-05): This issue was closed by revision r2240.
